description: Hey, I'm a full stack engineer, early career who has been in the startup space as soon as I graduated in 2025, and just love to build and explore my curiosity deeply in so many things. Excited to build something of value
summary:
TrailBlazer is a web-app built to drive object discovery and encourage collaboration. Data from the SPHEREx mission is mapped upfront and users can explore with an easy-to-use comparator for any patch of sky.

Within the software, the user can search a star name or RA/Dec, or click the all-sky map, and see every SPHEREx photo of that patch played in order as a time-lapse. The timelapse is built from live in the browser from NASA's public SPHEREx images, and on the timelapse, known asteroids and comets are labeled using SkyBoT, Gaia stars and checked against NASA's quality flags.

The whole purpose of the software is for the user to discover points of interest across the flat or 3D view of the sky constructed from SPHEREx sky tiles. Upon loading the region, the user will be able to compare different data layers. Afterwards, the user is able to tag their discovery in forums and comments, sharing their work with other users.
details:
TrailBlazer is a web-app used for driving discovery from SphereX data over periods of time. The more data that SphereX has for a selected patch of sky, the better chances of finding unknown objects.

Tools, languages, software

  • JavaScript, HTML, CSS, WebGL and three.js in the browser
  • Cloudflare Workers, D1 database, R2 storage and Turnstile
  • Python (astropy, numpy, reproject) for data prep and the detector; Playwright for interface tests
  • Data: NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx, JPL comet orbits, Gaia, 2MASS and WISE, SkyBoT, CDS Sesame
  • AI: Claude Code and Codex helped write and review the code
